# Agent Skills Doctor

Validate an existing Agent Skill against the agentskills.io specification
and best practices, report every finding with its check ID, and — when the
user asks — fix the findings and re-verify. Read-only by default: never
modify a skill unless the user explicitly asks for fixes.

## Workflow

- [ ] Step 1: Gather input — the path to the skill to validate.
- [ ] Step 2: Detect — run skillscheck and skills-ref when available, then
      the manual checklist.
- [ ] Step 3: Report — present findings grouped by severity with suggested
      fixes.
- [ ] Step 4: Fix — only when the user asks; auto-apply safe fixes, confirm
      judgment fixes.
- [ ] Step 5: Re-verify — re-run the linters and confirm findings are gone.

### Step 1: Gather input

You need one input: the **path to a skill directory** (or a `SKILL.md`
file). If the user has not provided one, ask. Do not guess which skill to
validate when several exist.

### Step 2: Detect

Run every check that is available, collecting findings with their check IDs:

1. **skillscheck** — primary linter. If `uvx` is installed, run
   `uvx skillscheck <skills-parent-dir>` (e.g. `uvx skillscheck skills` for
   `skills/<name>/`); otherwise run a `skillscheck` binary on `PATH`. Use
   `--format json` when you need to parse output programmatically. Exit code
   0 = no errors, 1 = errors. If neither is available, note the skip.
2. **skills-ref** — second automated check. If installed, run
   `skills-ref validate ./<name>` to verify frontmatter validity and naming
   conventions. Skip silently when not installed.
3. **Manual checklist** — re-read the target `SKILL.md` and check what the
   linters do not cover:
   - [ ] `name` matches the directory name and follows all naming rules
   - [ ] `description` is present, ≤ 1024 characters, states what + when,
         and uses agent-directed phrasing ("Use when <verb>ing...", not
         "when the user asks/wants/mentions")
   - [ ] Frontmatter is valid YAML with only spec-defined fields
   - [ ] Body is under 500 lines; detail lives in `references/` with
         explicit load triggers
   - [ ] Referenced file paths are relative and exist

For exact field constraints, naming rules, and token budgets, read
[references/specification.md](references/specification.md).

### Step 3: Report

Present findings grouped by severity — errors, then warnings, then info.
For each finding give:

- The check ID (e.g. `[2a.description.user-centric]`) when one exists
- The file and line
- What the rule is
- A concrete suggested fix

End the report by telling the user you can fix the findings on request.
Do not fix anything yet.

### Step 4: Fix

Only when the user explicitly asks ("fix it", "fix all", "fix the
description finding"). Read [references/fix-rules.md](references/fix-rules.md)
for per-finding fix guidance, then apply fixes in two tiers:

- **Safe tier — auto-apply without per-item confirmation.** Mechanical
  fixes: lowercase a `name`, collapse consecutive hyphens, rename a
  directory to match `name`, convert user-centric description phrasing to
  agent-directed form, trim an over-length `description`. Prefer
  `uvx skillscheck --fix` for what it covers, then hand-fix the rest.
- **Judgment tier — confirm before changing.** Rewrites and removals:
  rewriting a description, deleting orphaned files, moving content out of
  an over-long body into `references/`, changing metadata. Present the
  proposed change and get a "yes" per finding or a blanket "fix all".

Never touch files outside the target skill directory.

### Step 5: Re-verify

After fixing, re-run skillscheck (and skills-ref when available) on the
skill. Confirm every fixed finding is gone and no new findings appeared.
Report the final lint result and the list of applied changes to the user.

## Reference

- [references/specification.md](references/specification.md) — full
  agentskills.io field-by-field specification, script design rules, and
  eval guidance. Load when you need exact constraints.
- [references/fix-rules.md](references/fix-rules.md) — per-finding fix
  guidance keyed by skillscheck check ID. Load when the user asks to fix
  findings.

# Commit

Stage the current changes and create a git commit. All commit message
formatting rules (types, scopes, subject/body conventions) are defined in
the `commit-message` command — do NOT duplicate them here. This skill only
adds staging and committing on top.

## Steps

1. Run `git status --short` to see the current changes.
2. Stage the changes with `git add` — stage everything by default; if the
   user asked to commit only specific files, stage just those.
3. Run the `/commit-message` command to draft the commit message. Follow
   its output exactly — it defines the format, types, scopes, and style
   rules.
4. Show the drafted message to the user and ask for confirmation.
5. On confirmation, create the commit with `git commit -m "<message>"`.
   Quote the message safely and do not append any Co-Authored-By line.

## Rules

- Do NOT push the commit unless the user explicitly asks.
- Do NOT amend existing commits.
- Do NOT invent commit message rules — defer to the `commit-message` command.

# git-plugin

A Claude Code plugin that provides git-related commands and skills for streamlining development workflows.

## Commands

### `commit-message`

Drafts a [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) message for your current changes without staging files or running `git commit`.

**How it works:**

Gathers context by running `git status`, `git diff --staged`, `git diff`, and `git log` in parallel, then produces a commit message following these rules:

- **Format:** `<type>(<scope>): <subject>` with an optional one-sentence body
- **Types:** `feat`, `fix`, `refactor`, `chore`, `test`, `docs`, `style`
- **Scope:** inferred from changed file paths (omitted when multiple scopes apply)
- **Subject:** imperative mood, under 72 characters, no trailing period
- **Body:** explains *why*, not *what* — omitted when the subject is self-explanatory

**Output:** the commit message in a code block, ready to copy.

## Skills

### `commit`

Stages your current changes and creates a git commit. The commit message is drafted by the `commit-message` command — the skill only orchestrates staging and committing on top, without duplicating any message formatting rules.

**How it works:**

1. Shows current changes via `git status`.
2. Stages all changed files with `git add` (or only the files you specify).
3. Delegates message drafting to the `commit-message` command.
4. Asks for confirmation, then runs `git commit`.

### `agentskills-creator`

Creates a new Agent Skill following the [agentskills.io](https://agentskills.io) specification and best practices. If you haven't provided a name or purpose for the new skill, it asks for them before proceeding.

**How it works:**

1. Gathers the skill name and purpose (asks if missing).
2. Validates the name against the spec (lowercase, hyphens, matches the directory name).
3. Drafts a trigger-optimized `description` and confirms it with you.
4. Scaffolds `SKILL.md` (plus `scripts/`/`references/`/`assets/` only when needed), proposing the author metadata from existing skills for your confirmation (you can provide your own name) and starting at version `1.0.0`.
5. Writes the body following progressive-disclosure and instruction-design best practices.
6. Verifies the result by linting with [skillscheck](https://github.com/swival/skillscheck) when available (via `uvx`), plus a manual spec checklist.

The full field-by-field specification, script design rules, and eval workflows ship in `references/specification.md`, loaded on demand.

## Installation

This plugin is loaded automatically by Claude Code when placed in your project or global plugin directory. See the [Claude Code plugin documentation](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/claude-code/plugins) for setup details.

# Commit Message

Draft a conventional commit message for the current changes.
Do NOT run `git commit` or stage any files.

## Steps

Run these commands in parallel to gather the context:
- `git diff --staged`
- `git diff`
- `git status --short`

## Rules

**Format Without Body:**

```
<type>: <subject>
```

**Format With Optional Body:**

```
<type>: <subject>

<body>
```

Do NOT add a line break at the end the commit message. The commit message should not end with a newline character.

Do NOT run `git commit` or stage any files.

**Type**

Choose one of the following types:

- `feat` new feature
- `fix` bug fix
- `refactor` restructure without behavior change
- `chore` config, build, tooling, dependencies
- `test` Adding or updating tests
- `docs` Documentation only changes
- `style` Style and formatting only changes

**Scope**

Infer the scope from the following table of file paths. If the change touches multiple scopes or if no scope applies, omit it.

| File Path Pattern | Scope |
|-------------------|-------|
| `package.json`, `pyproject.toml` | `deps` |
| `*.md`, `doc/*` | `docs` |
| `test/` | `test` |
| `src/` | `feat` or `fix` |

**Subject:**

- Use Imperative mood ("add", not "added" or "adds")
- First line is less than 72 characters
- No period at the end
- Do NOT include the files changed or the details of the change in the subject line. Focus on the high-level change.
- Do NOT add a line break at the end the commit message. The commit message should not end with a newline character.

**Body (optional):**

- One sentence maximum
- Focus on *why* the change was made, not *what* changed
- Omit if the subject line is already self-explanatory
- Do NOT include the files changed or the details of the change in the body. Focus on the motivation for the change and any context that would be helpful for future maintainers.
- Do NOT add a line break at the end the commit message. The commit message should not end with a newline character.

## Output

Output only the final commit message, no explanation, no markdown fences, no Co-Authored-By line.
Output message in code block.

## Commit message checklist

- [ ] Type is appropriate (feat/fix/docs/etc.)
- [ ] Scope is specific and clear
- [ ] Summary is under 72 characters
- [ ] Summary uses imperative mood
- [ ] Body explains WHY not just WHAT
- [ ] Breaking changes are clearly marked
- [ ] Commit message does not end with a newline character or line break.

# Fix Rules for Agent Skills Findings

Per-finding fix guidance, keyed by skillscheck check ID where one exists.
Load this when the user asks to fix validation findings.

Two fix tiers:

- **Safe tier** — mechanical, behavior-preserving. Auto-apply without
  per-item confirmation.
- **Judgment tier** — rewrites or removals that change meaning. Confirm
  with the user before applying (per finding or a blanket "fix all").

Prefer `uvx skillscheck --fix` for the findings it auto-fixes, then
hand-fix the rest using the rules below.

## Spec compliance (category 1)

### Naming — `[1a.name.*]`

| Finding | Tier | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Uppercase in `name` | Safe | Lowercase it (`PDF-Processing` → `pdf-processing`). |
| Leading/trailing hyphen | Safe | Strip it (`-pdf` → `pdf`). |
| Consecutive hyphens | Safe | Collapse to one (`pdf--processing` → `pdf-processing`). |
| `name` ≠ directory name | Safe | Rename the directory to match `name` (or change `name` to match the directory — prefer renaming the directory, since the name is the public identifier). |
| Missing/empty `name` | Judgment | Derive from the directory name; confirm with the user. |

### Frontmatter — `[1b.frontmatter.*]`

| Finding | Tier | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Missing `description` | Judgment | Draft one from the body (imperative, what + when); confirm. |
| Invalid YAML | Judgment | Fix the syntax error; preserve all fields and values. |
| Unknown frontmatter field | Judgment | Move it under `metadata:` if it's a custom property, or remove it if redundant. Confirm before removing. |
| `description` over 1024 chars | Safe | Trim to ≤ 1024 by cutting redundant clauses; keep what + when + trigger keywords. |
| `compatibility` over 500 chars | Safe | Trim to the essential environment requirements. |

### `allowed-tools` — `[1c.allowed-tools.*]`

| Finding | Tier | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Unknown tool (`[1c.allowed-tools.unknown-tool]`) | Judgment | Usually a false positive from space-separated subcommand wildcards (`Bash(git status *)` splits into fragments). Leave as-is if the syntax matches the host agent's convention; otherwise rewrite to recognized tool names. Explain to the user before changing. |

### Cross-skill duplicates — `[1d.*]`

| Finding | Tier | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Duplicate skill names | Judgment | Determine which skill is canonical with the user; rename or remove the other. |

## Quality (category 2)

### Description — `[2a.description.*]`

| Finding | Tier | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| User-centric phrasing (`[2a.description.user-centric]`) | Safe | Convert to agent-directed form: "Use when the user asks/wants/mentions X" → "Use when <verb>ing X". E.g. "Use when the user asks to create a skill" → "Use when creating a skill". |
| Too short / missing "use when" hint | Judgment | Expand to state what the skill does AND when to use it, with trigger keywords. Confirm the rewrite. |
| Keyword-stuffing (`[2a.description.keyword-stuffing]`) | Judgment | Merge the comma-separated fragments into 1–2 sentences that explain what the skill does and when to activate it; keep the keywords as part of the prose. Confirm the rewrite. |

### Secrets and assets — `[2b.*]`, `[2c.*]`

| Finding | Tier | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Leaked secret (API key, token, private key, `.env`) | Judgment | Remove the secret immediately and replace with a placeholder; tell the user to rotate the credential. Never commit the real value. |
| Binary file in skill | Judgment | Confirm whether it's needed; remove or replace with a text/template equivalent. |
| Oversized asset | Judgment | Compress, split, or move to external storage; confirm. |

### Files and links — `[2d.*]`, `[2e.*]`

| Finding | Tier | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Extraneous root file (README, LICENSE, Makefile) | Judgment | Move license text into the `license` frontmatter field or a bundled file; remove build files. Confirm before deleting. |
| Orphaned file in `scripts/`/`references/`/`assets/` not referenced from `SKILL.md` | Judgment | Either reference it from `SKILL.md` with an explicit load trigger, or remove it. Confirm which. |
| Broken local markdown link | Safe | Fix the path to an existing file, or remove the link if the target is gone. |
| Broken fragment anchor | Safe | Fix the anchor to match an existing heading. |
| Unclosed code fence | Safe | Add the closing fence. |

## Progressive disclosure (category 3)

| Finding | Tier | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `SKILL.md` over 500 lines / token budget | Judgment | Move detail sections into `references/` and add explicit load triggers ("Read `references/x.md` when …"). Keep gotchas and the core workflow in `SKILL.md`. Confirm the split. |
| Reference file over token budget | Judgment | Split the reference into focused files; confirm. |
| Reference nesting too deep | Judgment | Flatten the reference tree; keep file references one level deep from `SKILL.md`. Confirm. |

## Agent compatibility (category 4)

| Finding | Tier | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Invalid agent config (`plugin.json`, `gemini-extension.json`, etc.) | Judgment | Fix the field to match the platform's schema; confirm. |
| Cross-agent field mismatch (name/version/description differ between config files) | Judgment | Align the fields to the canonical source (usually `SKILL.md` frontmatter); confirm. |
| Deprecated rules file (`.cursorrules`, `.roorules`, `.windsurfrules`) | Judgment | Migrate content into the platform's current convention; confirm. |

## After fixing

Re-run `uvx skillscheck <dir>` (and `skills-ref validate ./<name>` when
installed). Confirm every fixed finding is gone and no new findings were
introduced. Report the final result and the list of applied changes.

# Agent Skills Specification Reference

Complete format specification and creation guidance from
[agentskills.io](https://agentskills.io). Load this when you need exact
field constraints, validation rules, script design guidance, or eval
workflows.

## Directory structure

A skill is a directory containing, at minimum, a `SKILL.md` file:

```
skill-name/
├── SKILL.md          # Required: metadata + instructions
├── scripts/          # Optional: executable code
├── references/       # Optional: documentation
├── assets/           # Optional: templates, resources
└── ...               # Any additional files or directories
```

## `SKILL.md` format

YAML frontmatter followed by Markdown body. The body has no format
restrictions — write whatever helps the agent perform the task. Recommended
body sections: step-by-step instructions, input/output examples, common edge
cases.

### Frontmatter fields

| Field           | Required | Constraints |
| --------------- | -------- | ----------- |
| `name`          | Yes      | Max 64 chars. Lowercase letters, numbers, hyphens only. No leading/trailing hyphen. |
| `description`   | Yes      | Max 1024 chars. Non-empty. What the skill does and when to use it. |
| `license`       | No       | License name or reference to a bundled license file. |
| `compatibility` | No       | Max 500 chars. Environment requirements (product, system packages, network). |
| `metadata`      | No       | Arbitrary string→string map for extra metadata. |
| `allowed-tools` | No       | Space-separated pre-approved tools. (Experimental) |

Minimal example:

```markdown
---
name: skill-name
description: A description of what this skill does and when to use it.
---
```

Example with optional fields:

```markdown
---
name: pdf-processing
description: Extract PDF text, fill forms, merge files. Use when handling PDFs.
license: Apache-2.0
metadata:
  author: example-org
  version: "1.0"
---
```

### `name` field

- 1–64 characters
- Unicode lowercase alphanumeric (`a-z`, `0-9`) and hyphens (`-`) only
- Must not start or end with a hyphen
- Must not contain consecutive hyphens (`--`)
- Must match the parent directory name

Valid: `pdf-processing`, `data-analysis`, `code-review`
Invalid: `PDF-Processing` (uppercase), `-pdf` (leading hyphen),
`pdf--processing` (consecutive hyphens)

### `description` field

- 1–1024 characters
- Describe both what the skill does and when to use it
- Include specific keywords that help agents identify relevant tasks

Good: `Extracts text and tables from PDF files, fills PDF forms, and merges
multiple PDFs. Use when working with PDF documents or when the user mentions
PDFs, forms, or document extraction.`
Poor: `Helps with PDFs.`

### `license` field

Keep it short — a license name or the name of a bundled license file.
Example: `license: Proprietary. LICENSE.txt has complete terms`

### `compatibility` field

- 1–500 characters if provided
- Only include for specific environment requirements

Examples:

```yaml
compatibility: Designed for Claude Code (or similar products)
compatibility: Requires git, docker, jq, and access to the internet
compatibility: Requires Python 3.14+ and uv
```

Most skills do not need this field.

### `metadata` field

String→string map for properties not defined by the spec. Use reasonably
unique key names to avoid conflicts.

```yaml
metadata:
  author: example-org
  version: "1.0"
```

### `allowed-tools` field

Space-separated string of pre-approved tools. Experimental — support varies
between agent implementations.

```yaml
allowed-tools: Bash(git:*) Bash(jq:*) Read
```

## Progressive disclosure

Agents load skills progressively:

1. **Metadata** (~100 tokens): `name` and `description` loaded at startup
   for all skills.
2. **Instructions** (< 5000 tokens recommended): full `SKILL.md` body loaded
   on activation.
3. **Resources** (as needed): files in `scripts/`, `references/`, `assets/`
   loaded only when required.

Keep `SKILL.md` under 500 lines. Move detailed reference material to
separate files, and tell the agent *when* to load each one.

## Optional directories

### `scripts/`

Executable code agents can run. Scripts should be self-contained (or clearly
document dependencies), include helpful error messages, and handle edge
cases gracefully. Common languages: Python, Bash, JavaScript.

### `references/`

Documentation agents read when needed — `REFERENCE.md` (technical
reference), `FORMS.md` (form templates), or domain-specific files
(`finance.md`, `legal.md`). Keep individual files focused; smaller files
mean less context use.

### `assets/`

Static resources: templates, images, data files (lookup tables, schemas).

## File references

Use relative paths from the skill root. Keep references one level deep from
`SKILL.md` — avoid deeply nested reference chains.

```markdown
See [the reference guide](references/REFERENCE.md) for details.

Run the extraction script:
scripts/extract.py
```

## Validation

Two linters validate skills against the specification:

**skillscheck** (<https://github.com/swival/skillscheck>) — recommended.
Validates spec compliance (frontmatter, naming rules, directory-name
consistency, token budgets), quality (description length and "use when"
hints, user-centric phrasing, leaked secrets, broken links, orphaned files),
progressive disclosure (reference token budgets, nesting depth), and
agent-compatibility for Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, Cursor, Gemini CLI,
Roo Code, Swival, and Windsurf.

```bash
uvx skillscheck ./skills          # lint a skills directory
uvx skillscheck ./skills --strict # warnings count as errors (CI)
uvx skillscheck ./skills --format json
```

Exit codes: 0 = no errors, 1 = errors (or warnings with `--strict`).
Useful flags: `--fix` (safe mechanical fixes: lowercase names, collapse
consecutive hyphens, rename dirs to match `name`), `--agents`, `--check`.

**skills-ref** (<https://github.com/agentskills/agentskills/tree/main/skills-ref>) —
the official reference library. Checks that `SKILL.md` frontmatter is valid
and follows all naming conventions:

```bash
skills-ref validate ./my-skill
```

# Using scripts in skills

## One-off commands

When an existing package does what you need, reference it directly instead
of bundling a script. Pin versions for reproducibility and state
prerequisites in `SKILL.md` (or use the `compatibility` field).

- `uvx ruff@0.8.0 check .` — Python packages, requires uv
- `pipx run 'black==24.10.0' .` — Python packages, via OS package managers
- `npx eslint@9 --fix .` — npm packages, ships with Node.js
- `bunx eslint@9 --fix .` — Bun environments
- `deno run npm:create-vite@6 my-app` — Deno (permission flags required)
- `go run golang.org/x/tools/cmd/goimports@v0.28.0 .` — Go, built in

Move complex commands into bundled scripts — a tested script is more
reliable than a command that's hard to get right on the first try.

## Referencing scripts from `SKILL.md`

List available scripts so the agent knows they exist, then instruct the
agent to run them. Paths in code blocks are relative to the skill directory
root (the agent runs commands from there):

```markdown
## Available scripts

- **`scripts/validate.sh`** — Validates configuration files

## Workflow

1. Run the validation script:
   bash scripts/validate.sh "$INPUT_FILE"
```

## Self-contained scripts

Declare dependencies inline so the script runs with a single command:

- **Python (PEP 723)**: TOML block in `# ///` markers; run with
  `uv run scripts/extract.py`. Pin with PEP 508 specifiers
  (`"beautifulsoup4>=4.12,<5"`), constrain with `requires-python`.
- **Deno**: `npm:`/`jsr:` import specifiers; run with
  `deno run scripts/extract.ts`.
- **Bun**: version in the import path (`from "cheerio@1.0.0"`); run with
  `bun run scripts/extract.ts`. Auto-install disabled if a `node_modules`
  exists up the tree.
- **Ruby**: `bundler/inline` with a `gemfile do` block; pin versions
  explicitly.

## Designing scripts for agentic use

Agents read stdout/stderr to decide next steps. Design accordingly:

- **No interactive prompts** (hard requirement) — agents cannot answer TTY
  prompts. Accept all input via flags, env vars, or stdin. Fail with a clear
  usage message when required args are missing.
- **Document with `--help`** — brief description, flags, usage examples.
  This is the primary way an agent learns the interface. Keep it concise.
- **Helpful errors** — say what went wrong, what was expected, what to try:
  `Error: --format must be one of: json, csv, table. Received: "xml"`.
- **Structured output** — JSON/CSV/TSV over free-form text; composable with
  `jq`/`cut`/`awk`. Data to stdout, diagnostics to stderr.
- **Idempotency** — agents may retry. "Create if not exists" beats "create
  and fail on duplicate."
- **Reject ambiguous input** — clear errors over guessing; use enums/closed
  sets.
- **Dry-run support** — `--dry-run` for destructive or stateful operations.
- **Meaningful exit codes** — distinct codes per failure type, documented in
  `--help`.
- **Safe defaults** — destructive ops may need `--confirm`/`--force`.
- **Predictable output size** — harnesses truncate large output. Default to
  summaries; support `--offset` pagination or require `--output` for large
  results.

# Best practices for skill creators

## Start from real expertise

Don't generate skills from general training knowledge alone — the result is
vague ("handle errors appropriately"). Ground skills in real expertise:

- **Extract from a hands-on task**: complete a real task with an agent, then
  extract the reusable pattern. Capture steps that worked, corrections you
  made, input/output formats, and context the agent didn't know.
- **Synthesize from project artifacts**: internal docs, runbooks, style
  guides, API specs, code review comments, git history, real failure cases.

## Refine with real execution

Run the skill against real tasks and feed results (not just failures) back
into revision. Read execution traces, not just final outputs — wasted steps
usually mean instructions are too vague, inapplicable, or offer too many
options without a default.

## Spending context wisely

- **Add what the agent lacks, omit what it knows.** Ask of each piece:
  "Would the agent get this wrong without this instruction?" If no, cut it.
  If the agent handles the whole task well without the skill, the skill may
  not add value.
- **Design coherent units** — like scoping a function: encapsulate one
  coherent unit of work that composes with other skills.
- **Aim for moderate detail** — concise stepwise guidance with a working
  example outperforms exhaustive documentation.
- **Structure large skills with progressive disclosure** — core instructions
  in `SKILL.md`; detail in `references/` with explicit load triggers.

## Calibrating control

- **Match specificity to fragility** — freedom (with the *why*) where
  approaches vary; exact prescribed sequences where operations are fragile.
  Most skills mix both; calibrate each part independently.
- **Provide defaults, not menus** — one default, alternatives as brief
  escape hatches.
- **Favor procedures over declarations** — reusable methods over one-off
  answers.

## Patterns for effective instructions

- **Gotchas sections** — concrete, environment-specific facts that defy
  reasonable assumptions (soft-delete columns, mismatched ID names across
  services, misleading health endpoints). Keep in `SKILL.md`. When you
  correct an agent mistake, add it to gotchas.
- **Templates for output format** — concrete structures beat prose
  descriptions. Short ones inline; long ones in `assets/`.
- **Checklists for multi-step workflows** — explicit `- [ ]` steps when
  steps have dependencies or validation gates.
- **Validation loops** — do work → run validator → fix → repeat until pass.
  A reference document can serve as the validator.
- **Plan-validate-execute** — for batch/destructive operations: produce a
  structured plan, validate it against a source of truth with a script, then
  execute. Error messages should let the agent self-correct.
- **Bundle reusable scripts** — if the agent reinvents the same logic across
  runs, write a tested script once and bundle it in `scripts/`.

# Optimizing skill descriptions

Agents typically consult skills only for tasks needing knowledge beyond
their own — specialized APIs, domain workflows, uncommon formats. The
description carries the entire triggering burden.

Principles:

- **Imperative phrasing** — "Use this skill when...".
- **User intent over implementation.**
- **Err pushy** — include contexts where the user doesn't name the domain.
- **Keep concise** — a few sentences to a short paragraph; hard limit 1024
  chars.

## Trigger evals

Build ~20 eval queries in `eval_queries.json`
(`{"query": ..., "should_trigger": true|false}`): 8–10 should-trigger,
8–10 should-not. Vary phrasing (formal/casual/typos), explicitness (naming
the domain vs. describing the need), detail, and complexity. The best
should-trigger queries are ones where the connection isn't obvious. The best
negative queries are near-misses sharing keywords but needing something
different. Include realistic context: file paths, personal backstory,
specific values.

Run each query 3+ times (nondeterminism) and compute trigger rates.
Should-trigger passes above ~0.5; should-not-trigger passes below.

Split queries into train (~60%) and validation (~40%) sets to avoid
overfitting. Optimize against train only; select the best iteration by
validation pass rate. When revising: broaden scope for missed triggers, add
specificity/negative boundaries for false triggers, and avoid adding literal
keywords from failed queries (that's overfitting). ~5 iterations is usually
enough.

# Evaluating skill output quality

## Test cases

Store in `evals/evals.json` inside the skill directory. Each case: `id`,
`prompt` (realistic user message), `expected_output` (human-readable success
criteria), optional `files`. Start with 2–3 cases; vary phrasing and
formality; cover at least one edge case; use realistic context.

## Running evals

Run each case twice — **with the skill** and **without it** (baseline) — in
clean contexts (subagents or fresh sessions). Organize results in a
workspace: `iteration-N/eval-<name>/{with_skill,without_skill}/outputs/`.
Record `timing.json` (tokens, duration) per run. When improving an existing
skill, snapshot the old version and use it as the baseline.

## Assertions and grading

Add assertions after seeing first outputs. Good assertions are verifiable,
specific, countable ("The output file is valid JSON", "at least 3
recommendations"). Avoid vague ("output is good") or brittle (exact phrase)
checks. Grade each PASS/FAIL with concrete evidence quoted from the output —
no benefit of the doubt. Use scripts for mechanical checks, LLM judgment for
the rest. For comparing versions, blind comparison (judge doesn't know which
output came from which version) complements assertion grading.

## Aggregating and iterating

Compute `benchmark.json` per iteration: pass rate, time, tokens per
configuration, plus deltas. The delta tells you what the skill costs and
buys. Then:

- Drop assertions that always pass in both configurations (no signal).
- Fix assertions that always fail in both (broken test, wrong check).
- Study assertions that pass with skill but fail without (the skill's value).
- Tighten instructions when results are inconsistent across runs.
- Check time/token outliers by reading execution transcripts.

Review outputs with a human and record specific, actionable feedback per
test case. Iterate: give failed assertions + feedback + transcripts +
current `SKILL.md` to an LLM and ask for improvements. Generalize from
feedback (no narrow patches), keep the skill lean (removing instructions
often helps), explain the *why* in instructions, and bundle repeated work
into scripts. Repeat until satisfied or improvements plateau.
